subject: arch/arm64/src/imx9/imx9_lpi2c.c: Fix bus reset
label: not_needed_hw
evidence: The listed hunks rewrite imx9_lpi2c_reset: the commit message says the old GPIO recovery 'tried to toggle scl line as GPIO, but the line was not even muxed properly' and replaces it with relaxed mode plus address-0 start/stop sequences, stating '"Relaxed mode" is a new feature on the LPI2C block used in imx93'; the config-table hunks only drop reset_scl_pin/reset_sda_pin, which the rewrite no longer uses. The new code depends on LPI2C_MCFG0_RELAX (MCFGR0 bit 16), which the imx9 header defines, while the imxrt LPI2C header (included unconditionally by imxrt_lpi2c.c for every imxrt family) stops the MCFGR0 bits at RDMO (bit 9) followed by 'Bits 31-10 Reserved', and nothing under arch/arm/src/imxrt defines an LPI2C relax bit, so the fix cannot be carried over. The stated root cause does not appear on imxrt either: imxrt_lpi2c_reset configures the reset pins with imxrt_config_gpio(reset_scl_pin | GPIO_SION_ENABLE), and imxrt_config_gpio muxes the pad itself (imxrt_gpio_configinput writes PADMUX_MUXMODE_ALT5 plus SION into the pad mux register; the RT118x RGPIO variant calls imxrt_iomux_configure(pinset) first), so the pads are switched to GPIO before they are toggled and read back. The remaining part of the hunk (re-initialising the port even when recovery fails) is already present on imxrt, where the out: label now sits before imxrt_lpi2c_init (later commit 70e453c2c 'Improve imxrt_lpi2c_reset').

evidence_refs.quote: #define LPI2C_MCFG0_RDMO (1 << 9) /* Receive Data Match Only Bit */

subject: arch/arm/nrf52: Fix nxstyle errors in nrf52_usbd.c.
label: not_a_fix
evidence: The commit message describes the change as style only: 'Indent the case labels of the two switches in nrf52_ep0out_stdrequest() one level in from the switch body's brace, and wrap the lines that then exceed the limit, so the file passes checkpatch. Whitespace only: xiao-nrf52840:usbnsh builds to the same nuttx.bin.' The single listed hunk re-indents the case labels of the standard-request switch and wraps long usbtrace/nrf52_ep_findbyaddr lines; comparing the commit with whitespace ignored leaves only those line wraps, with identical tokens, so no behaviour changes. The other side's nrf54l_ep0out_stdrequest already uses the indented case-label layout that the nrf52 commit adopts, so there is nothing to carry over in any case.

subject: arch/arm64/src/imx9/imx9_usbdev.c: Fix the descriptor alignments and cache management
label: not_needed_absent
evidence: The commit ('Align all the dtd and dqh on cache line boundaries and clean up the cache management') fixes DMA/cache coherency in the imx9 controller: the listed hunks add ARMV8A cache-line macros, make the endpoint transfer descriptors (dTD) and queue heads (dQH) cache-line aligned, and invalidate the EP0 DMA buffer priv->ep0.buf before handing it to CLASS_SETUP in imx9_dispatchrequest. lpc214x_usbdev.c has none of this: its device structure has no dQH/dTD arrays (besides status fields it holds only the endpoint list and, under CONFIG_LPC214X_USBDEV_DMA, a dmadesc pointer), there are no cache macros or cache maintenance calls anywhere in the file, and its only DMA descriptor type (lpc214x_dmadesc_s in dedicated USB RAM) sits behind CONFIG_LPC214X_USBDEV_DMA, which stops the build with '# error DMA SUPPORT NOT YET FULLY IMPLEMENTED'. Endpoint data is moved by the CPU through the RXDATA/TXDATA registers (lpc214x_epread/lpc214x_epwrite), so no DMA engine writes RAM behind the cache. The corresponding lpc214x_dispatchrequest passes no buffer at all (CLASS_SETUP(..., ctrl, NULL, 0)), so there is no EP0 buffer that could need invalidating.

evidence_refs.quote: # error DMA SUPPORT NOT YET FULLY IMPLEMENTED

subject: arch/{nrf52|nrf53}/usbd: various fixes to improve USB stability
label: not_needed_hw
evidence: The commit (identical hunks in nrf52_usbd.c and nrf53_usbd.c) works around the nRF USBD's EasyDMA, which its message describes as 'only one EasyDMA channel which must be shared for all EPs' and 'only one DMA transfer can take place at a time'; three of the four listed hunks are that arbitration (the NRF52_TRACEERR_DMABUSY trace code, the NRF52_USBD_DMAIRQ mask built from the nRF ENDEPIN/ENDEPOUT/ENDISOIN/ENDISOOUT events, and the dmaepinwait/dmaepoutwait waiting bitsets). The n32h7 USBHS device driver has nothing of this: it moves data through per-endpoint FIFOs (n32_txfifo_write writes words to N32_USBHS_DFIFO_DEP, n32_rxfifo_read reads them), never enables the core's DMA mode or uses its DMA address registers, and nothing under arch/arm/src/n32h7 refers to ENDEPIN/ENDEPOUT events or a shared DMA channel, so there is no single DMA engine to arbitrate. The remaining hunk, sending a zero-length packet when an IN request has len == 0 (plus the EasyDMA ack), is already handled on n32h7: n32_epin_request sets privep->zlp when privreq->req.len == 0, enters the transfer branch because of the zlp flag, and n32_epin_transfer programs PKTCNT = 1 with a zero transfer size for nbytes == 0.

subject: arch/risc-v: fix uninitialized HW cmds and bus clock
label: already_ok
evidence: The fix in esp_i2c.c zero-initialises the i2c_ll_hw_cmd_t bit-field structs in esp_i2c_sendstart/esp_i2c_startrecv (commit message: 'so ack_exp/done are not left with stack garbage that can NACK or skip the address byte') and makes esp_i2c_init_clock pass the requested bus_freq to i2c_hal_set_bus_timing() instead of priv->config->clk_freq ('instead of the board default so msg frequency is applied'). The legacy esp32c3_i2c.c never had either problem because it does not use the HAL command structs: esp32c3_i2c_sendstart and esp32c3_i2c_startrecv write whole command words built by the I2C_BASE_CMD / I2C_SEND_CMD / I2C_RECV_CMD macros, which compute every bit from explicit operands (opcode, ack check or ack value, byte count), so no field can carry stale stack data. Its esp32c3_i2c_init_clock derives all bus timing (clock divider, half cycle, SCL periods) from its bus_freq argument and stores priv->clk_freq = bus_freq, and esp32c3_i2c_transfer calls it with msgs[i].frequency for every message, so the per-message frequency is already applied.

subject: arch: cxd56xx: Fix bug when watchdog restart
label: not_needed_hw
evidence: The two main hunks add a write to CXD56_WDT_WDOGINTCLR before the counter is re-enabled in cxd56_start and cxd56_settimeout; the commit message says this fixes 'a bug that watchdog is expired in less time than the specified time when restarting without clearing interrupt', which comes from the cxd56 watchdog's two-lap scheme (interrupt on the first lap, reset on the second) and its write-only Clear Interrupt register. The SAMA5 WDT is a different peripheral: hardware/sam_wdt.h defines only the CR, MR and SR registers (restart through WDT_CR_WDRSTT plus a key, underflow and error flags in SR) and has no interrupt-clear, load or lock register, and sam_wdt.c notes that WDT_MR can be written only once and that writing it reloads the timer. Accordingly sam_start writes no register at all (it only returns priv->started ? OK : -ENOSYS) and sam_settimeout writes WDT_MR once, so there is no restart path that could leave a stale first-lap interrupt pending and nothing equivalent to WDOGINTCLR to write. The remaining hunk only corrects a debug format string in cxd56_getreg ('%08' to '%08x'), which is a logging change; sam_getreg has a similarly malformed '%048' specifier, but it is debug-only output under CONFIG_SAMA5_WDT_REGDEBUG and does not change device behaviour.

evidence_refs.quote: The Watchdog Mode Register (WDT_MR) can be written only once.
Writing the WDT_MR register reloads the
two laps until reset signal is asserted. At 1st lap, interrupt signal
cxd56_putreg(0, CXD56_WDT_WDOGINTCLR); /* reload by write any value */

subject: xtensa/esp32s3: Fix static_assert compilation error
label: not_needed_absent
evidence: The single listed hunk only adds the message argument to the static_assert at the top of esp32s3's esp_setup_syscall_table; the commit title calls it a fix for a 'static_assert compilation error', i.e. a build fix for the one-argument form. The esp32s2 copy of esp_setup_syscall_table contains no static_assert at all: it only points syscall_table_ptr_pro at g_stub_table and assigns the Newlib 3.0.0 ROM lock symbols __sinit_recursive_mutex and __sfp_recursive_mutex, and a search of arch/xtensa/src/esp32s2 finds no static_assert and no use of struct __lock anywhere. The esp32s3 assertion guards the size of struct __lock for the ROM's retargetable-locking hooks (_retarget_lock_* in the esp32s3 ROM header), whereas the esp32s2 ROM header defines _lock_t as int and exposes the older _lock_init/_lock_acquire hooks, so the esp32s2 file has no statement that could fail to build in this way.

evidence_refs.quote: /* Newlib 3.0.0 is used in ROM, the following lock symbols are defined: */

subject: arch/arm/stm32: fix stm32f1xx alarm support Summary: stm32: support querying a previously set RTC alarm In the STM32F1xx series
label: already_ok
evidence: The listed hunk is an STM32F1 build fix in the lower half shared by several STM32 families: stm32_rdalarm compared the alarm ID with RTC_ALARMA/RTC_ALARMB, which only the F4 and L15 alarm headers provide, while the F1 header stm32_alarm.h had no such IDs and no rdalarm backend (the same commit adds struct alm_rdalarm_s and stm32_rtc_rdalarm there); the commit message says enabling CONFIG_RTC_ALARM on STM32F1 gave 'an error ... due to the inability to find the specific implementation of rdalarm', and the hunk keeps the ALARMA/ALARMB check only for F4/L15 and accepts IDs below CONFIG_RTC_NALARMS otherwise. The esp32c3-legacy counterpart rtc_lh_rdalarm never used family-specific alarm names: it checks the ID against RTC_ALARM0 and RTC_ALARM_LAST from its own enum alm_id_e, which esp32c3_rtc.h defines under the same CONFIG_RTC_ALARM guard as the function, and it reads the alarm through up_rtc_rdalarm, which esp32c3_rtc.h declares and esp32c3_rtc.c implements. So with CONFIG_RTC_ALARM enabled every symbol it uses exists and the accepted IDs match what its backend supports; the way it is written never had this problem. One unrelated difference is that it checks the ID range only with DEBUGASSERT rather than a runtime if, but this commit did not change that aspect (the pre-fix STM32 code already had a runtime check).

subject: stm32h7:Serial Fix Logic error in up_dma_txavailable
label: not_needed_absent
evidence: The hunk fixes a real logic error in stm32h7's up_dma_txavailable (commit title 'Serial Fix Logic error in up_dma_txavailable'): '(priv->dev.dmatx.length && priv->dev.dmatx.nlength) == 0' is true whenever either segment length is zero, so a new TX DMA could be started while part of the previous split transfer was still pending, and the fix requires both lengths to be zero. lpc214x_serial.c has no TX DMA path at all: its uart_ops_s table registers only setup, shutdown, attach, detach, ioctl, receive, rxint, rxavailable, send, txint, txready and txempty (no dmasend, dmatxavail or similar), and transmission is done byte by byte by uart_xmitchars from up_interrupt on the THRE interrupt. A case-insensitive search for 'dma' under arch/arm/src/lpc214x finds only USB device register definitions in lpc214x_usbdev.h, nothing in the serial driver, so there is no dmatx bookkeeping on this side that could be tested wrongly.

subject: arch/arm/imxrt: fix eDMA NCE error caused by zero-length split transfer
label: not_needed_absent
evidence: The listed hunk adds 'dev->dmatx.nlength > 0' to the split-transfer test in imxrt_dma_send so that no chained eDMA TCD is set up with iter == 0; the commit message says 'Chaining a TCD with iter == 0 causes eDMA NCE errors and halts the eDMA engine when HOE is enabled'. mx8mp_serial.c has no DMA transmit path: its uart_ops_s table registers only setup, shutdown, attach, detach, ioctl, receive, rxint, rxavailable, send, txint, txready and txempty (no dmasend or dmatxavail), and transmission is done by uart_xmitchars from mx8mp_interrupt when TRDY is set and TXEMPTYEN is enabled. A case-insensitive search for 'dma' in mx8mp_serial.c finds nothing, and arch/arm/src/mx8mp contains no DMA driver at all (no edma or sdma source file; the only DMA mentions are an unused SDMA1 clock-gate index in hardware/mx8mp_ccm.h and SDMA event pin-mux definitions), so there is no TCD chaining or dmatx.nbuffer handling on this side that could hit the zero-length case.
